target: Let E be a real normed space with its original norm and let e:E to R^d be an algebraic linear equivalence. Let f:E to EReal be proper, V convex, and lambda>=0. Assume that at EVERY p in V the actual GLOBAL subdifferential of u maps to f(e inverse u) at e(p) is nonempty. Then the exact strong interpolation inequality with penalty (lambda/2)a(1-a)||x-y||_E^2 is equivalent to f(p)+<g,e(q-p)>+(lambda/2)||q-p||_E^2<=f(q) for every p,q in V and every global coordinate subgradient g at p. Feasible values are proved finite internally, so the Lean right side uses toReal without assigning an infinite value a misleading real zero. This is the full Lemma4.2 iff under its printed V subset dom partial f premise, represented by explicit algebraic coordinates. Properness comes from Definition4.1; it means no bottom anywhere and a genuine finite real witness somewhere. The all-point support premise is supplied, not proved by this theorem. No separate V subset effectiveDomain premise is added: derive it using subgradient_point_finite after transporting properness through e inverse. No isometry or Euclidean penalty substitution is allowed. This is finite-dimensional coordinate representation, not an infinite-dimensional iff claim. Empty V, lambda0 and d0 are allowed by the core statement. Closedness, global convexity of f and minimizer attainment are not assumed.
